answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents must stake scarce assets like tokenized timber or saffron before validating actions. Malicious or duplicated identities trigger cryptographic stake burning, forcing an exponential loss penalty. Verification networks mirror identity graphs to impose superlinear cost scaling: registering $k$ coordinated clones scales slashable deposits at $O(k^2)$, making widespread economic manipulation mathematically unviable.
